title: Real lab: find the needle with grep
instruction: Real Linux box. The folder /data has a bunch of files. Some contain the word 'apple'. Count HOW MANY files under /data contain 'apple', and write just that number into /root/answer. Then click Verify.
setup:
mkdir -p /data; printf 'i like apple pie
' > /data/a.txt; printf 'bananas
' > /data/b.txt; printf 'APPLE in caps and apple lower
' > /data/c.txt; printf 'cherry
' > /data/d.txt; printf 'pineapple counts too
' > /data/e.txt; echo '(scenario ready: files are in /data)'

verify.command: if [ "$(cat /root/answer 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')" = 3 ]; then echo SEARCH_OK; else echo SEARCH_NO got=$(cat /root/answer 2>/dev/null); fi
verify.success: Solved! `grep -rl apple /data | wc -l` = 3 (a.txt, c.txt, e.txt, case-sensitive grep skips the all-caps APPLE, but 'pineapple' contains 'apple'). grep -r searches recursively, -l lists matching files.
verify.fail: Not yet. Count files under /data containing 'apple' (lowercase) and put the number in /root/answer. There are 3.
